title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-lee-2026-04-01
content:
Objective: capture breadcrumbs for recurring NaN/quality regressions after moving some models to INT8/FP8 profiles. This is a personal scratchpad  messy notes, commands tried, and hypotheses.

Summary of the problem:
- Intermittent NaNs in generation for some LLMs (mostly Llama-family forks and a couple of Flan variants) when served with INT8 or FP8 quantized kernels.
- Failures mostly show up after ~50-200 tokens generated (post-kv-cache growth). Sometimes manifests as immediate hallucinated tokens / sudden drop in log-probs before NaN.
- Repro on local A100 and H100 training infra, not only in prod.

Environment snapshot:
- PyTorch 2.1.0+cu118
- transformers 4.35.2
- bitsandbytes 0.41.0
- custom runtime branch: serving-runtime/quant-opt-2026-03 (PR linked above)
- CUDA 11.8, cuBLAS 11.x, NCCL 2.18
- Models: redwood/llama-65b-opt (fp16 baseline), experimental-quantized variants: int8, fp8-e4m3, bf16 fallback

Quick repro commands tried (local):
1) baseline (fp16):
  python run_inference.py --model redwood/llama-65b-opt --dtype fp16 --device cuda:0 --prompt "<long prompt>" --max-tokens 256
  -> works, no NaNs, deterministic across seeds (seed=42)

2) int8 runtime (bitsandbytes load):
  python run_inference.py --model redwood/llama-65b-opt --quantize int8 --bnb-use-8bit --device cuda:0 --prompt "<long prompt>" --max-tokens 256 --seed 42
  -> intermittent NaN at step ~87 on A100. Stack shows matmul op returning NaN.
  Error snippet: "RuntimeError: output contains NaN (detected at /opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_167289.../aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Blas.cpp:402)"

3) fp8 emulation (software FP8 fallback):
  python run_inference.py --model redwood/llama-65b-opt --quantize fp8 --fp8-mode e4m3 --device cuda:0 --prompt "<prompt>" --max-tokens 256
  -> often fails earlier (token 30-60). Observed large gradients/values in attention that look suspicious.

4) bf16 mixed (force bf16 for linear matmuls, keep kv cache in fp16):
  export TORCH_USE_BF16=1
  python run_inference.py --model ... --dtype bf16 --device cuda:0
  -> more stable but reduced sample quality vs fp16 baseline (some label drift). No NaNs in many runs.

Commands added for instrumentation:
- Inserted checks in runtime after matmul / add operations to assert not torch.isnan(...). Use an ENV var to toggle heavy assertions: RUNTIME_ASSERT_NAN=1
- Dumped the KV cache (first 10 layers) on failure to s3/local with index and token position. Format: layerN_tokenT_fp16.npy
- Added RNG seed logging and deterministic cudnn settings for repro: torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True, cudnn.benchmark=False

Observations from dumps:
- On failing runs, attention scores for some heads explode to very large magnitudes before softmax, producing inf/nan when exponentiated. The pattern: one head in middle layers (layers 18-22) has values ~1e6.
- The KV cache entries at the corresponding positions sometimes contain NaN in a small subset of channels (not entire vector). This suggests corruption at storage or during matmul accumulation rather than a single catastrophic step.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization scale calibration is insufficient for some layers (per-tensor quantization causes overflow when sequence length grows). Per-channel quantization would help.
2) Accumulation precision: int8 kernels are using float16 accumulation in some fused kernels leading to overflow for long sequences  need float32 accumulation or Kahan style.
3) KV cache write path is using an unsafe cast in the fast path (e.g., downcast from fp32->int8->fp16) and certain alignment on H100 triggers vectorized stores that produce NaN when not 32-byte aligned.
4) FP8 exponent bias handling bug in our emulation (edge case for extremely negative/positive exponents).
5) Race condition in async copy / compute overlap that sometimes writes into buffer while it's read (seen on multi-stream path in serving runtime).

Quick experiments and results:
- Per-channel quantization (experimental API):
  python run_inference.py --model ... --quantize int8 --quant-scheme per_channel --calib-samples 32
  -> reduced frequency of NaN, still reproducible with a specific prompt. Suggests scale is contributor.

- Force float32 accumulation in GEMM (set env GEMM_ACCUM_TYPE=float32 in custom kernel):
  -> eliminated NaNs in local repro for >10 runs. Performance drop ~8-12% but stable. Strong evidence accumulation precision matters.

- Disable async KV writes (force synchronous path):
  -> still saw NaN in one run. Lowers probability but not eliminating. So race is possible but not only cause.

- FP8 library tests: run unit tests for fp8 encode/decode across edge ranges (max exponent ranges, NaN payloads). Found a bug in e4m3 decode when input is exactly 0x7f (edge case)  patch applied in branch fp8-fix-2026-03. After patch, fp8 failure rate decreased but not eliminated.

Instrumentation traces (short):
- At token 86: head_19 pre-softmax max=1.2e6, min=-1e2
- matmul A (shape: 2048x512) -> B (512x2048) accumulate -> output contain inf in channel indices [345,678]
- KV cache layer19 token86 channel345 = NaN (first NaN observed)

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Run a matrix of accumulation type vs quantization scheme vs hardware (A100/H100). Create a small job matrix: {accum=float32,float16} x {quant=per-tensor,per-channel} x {hw=A100,H100} and log NaN rate. (Owner: Lee)
- [ ] Add lightweight per-layer scale monitoring (log scale histograms) in prod for top 10 models to detect layers approaching overflow. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Push the GEMM_accum=float32 safe mode behind a config flag in serving-runtime and enable for model groups where we see NaN flaps. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Add a sanity write-read test for KV cache path that runs on startup of dedicated nodes to ensure alignment and no overlapping access. (Owner: Dev)
- [ ] Follow up on fp8 decode patch; run exhaustive encode/decode roundtrips for e4m3 across random floats + edgecases. (Owner: Lee/Maya)

Notes / random thoughts:
- The fact BF16 mixed path is stable suggests that preserving higher accumulation precision (even if storage is lower precision) helps. The kernels that fused quantize+matmul may be the culprits.
- Consider using dynamic or mixed accumulation: keep accumulation in fp32 for the first N tokens (cold start) then allow fp16 later. Might reduce perf cost while keeping safety.
- Add a "graceful degrade" policy in routing: if a model shows >X NaN rate in last Y requests, route to fp16 baseline variant automatically. This ties into console rollouts/Optimize.

Useful snippets saved here for easy copy: 
- Dump KV cache (torch):
  def dump_kv(layer_idx, token_idx, kv):
      np.save(f"/tmp/kv_dump/l{layer_idx}_t{token_idx}.npy", kv.cpu().numpy())

- Quick check: show first NaN index printed in runtime after matmul:
  nan_idx = torch.isnan(out).nonzero(as_tuple=False)
  if nan_idx.numel():
      print(f"NaN at layer {layer} token {token_pos} idx {nan_idx[0].tolist()}")

- Profiling command (nsys):
  nsys profile --output=profile_run --trace=cuda,cudnn python run_inference.py --model ... --quantize int8 --max-tokens 256

References and reading:
- internal confluence: quantization-playbooks (linked)
- bitsandbytes issues: https://github.com/facebookresearch/bitsandbytes/issues/321
- fp8 emulation notes from NVIDIA SDK

Contact: ping me in #eng-quant (Slack) if you want the raw dumps. Will incrementally move reproducer into infra job once matrix completes.

End of scratchpad.
